newsitem.title: USA: NY PRECIOUS METALS END MIXED AFTER NERVOUS DAY.
newsitem.headline: NY PRECIOUS METALS END MIXED AFTER NERVOUS DAY.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday, after a choppy trading session, in which gold and silver tracked the volatile action in U.S. bonds and stocks and the U.S. dollar.
"Basically gold and silver followed the stocks and bonds, but it was a nervous day," said CTA and COMEX floor trader, John Giapoutzis of Dynamic Market Research in New York.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average made new intraday lows for the fourth day in a row Wednesday, after hitting a new record high last week intraweek, and then closing lower than the previous week, something which has happened only nine times since 1970.
"Initially the surprise today was the PPI which was down, and a lot of people got short in gold, as stocks and bonds rallied, but they then had to cover as when the rally in the Dow failed," he said.
The U.S. July PPI fell 0.1 pct, the seventh consecutive monthly decline, calming some of the inflation fears which had contributed to the past week's sharp downward correction in bonds and stocks.
On Thursday the U.S. July CPI is due with a rise of 0.2 pct expected.
"Most inflation analysts keep pointing to lagging indices of inflation to prove there are no price pressures in the economy," Steven Jon Kaplan, editor of the "Gold Mining Outlook" said.
"Perhaps they drive their automobiles by keeping their eyes firmly on the rear view mirror - eventually they'll crash into something," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down 10 cents at $330.70 an ounce, after seeing a session high at $333.20, not far from the top of the month old range around $335.00.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted around $326.90/40 an ounce, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $326.20, the New York close Tuesday around $324.80.

Implied gold lease rates rose sharply again Wednesday, to 2.29 pct for one month from 1.93 pct Tuesday, and to 2.26 percent for one year from 2.20 pct, suggesting funds and producers may be borrowing again to fund short positions and hedges, with gold back near the top of its range of the past month around $330.00 in the spot market.

Producers are lining up to sell again above the top of the month old range in COMEX December gold around $335.00 an ounce, but funds would likely want to cover more short positions on a serious upside break above $335.00, and there have been no indications of central bank activity in recent weeks, analysts said.

"Surely after seeing the unexpectedly sharp declines in several of the so-called invincible tiger securities of the developing Asian countries, not to mention the slow collapse in the traditionally reliable German deutchmark, central banks which were considering selling gold to purchase 'safe' time deposits have been rethinking this strategy," Kaplan said.
COMEX September silver ended up 8.2 cent at $4.507 an ounce, after testing the high of the past month around $4.540.

But NYMEX October platinum ended down $3.90 at $431.10, while NYMEX September palladium closed off $2.15 an ounce at $215.85, as both contracts continued to consolidate after seeing new contract highs earlier this month.
"October platinum has shown its strong structure with the ability to return to strength after a sizable washout," CRB analyst Terry Roggensack said.
"Longer term target upside in the platinum are $464.00 and $471.00."
Meanwhile, the acute shortage of metal in the physical market continued, with one month platinum lease rates around 20 pct and one month palladium still around 80 pct, refining sources said.
